correctness.rationale: Adjoin equality at level 0 and the total relation at level h=K+1. The three pairwise merger levels determine every pure atom, with level 0 recognizing repetitions. For distinct entries the largest level occurs at least twice by transitivity and nesting. The ordered count is thus 1 all-equal, 3h one-repeated-pair, h equilateral, and 3·binom(h,2) one-closer-pair types. All are realized on the proposed comb: at level j its two new leaves and an older leaf give an equilateral triple, and the older cluster supplies a pair with any earlier merger i. Every universal class tree has at least one node with three children at each of the h levels, each contributing at least two to leaves minus one. Equality forces exactly one ternary branch at every level and no other branching. A type (i,j,j) then places the unique level-i branching node strictly below the unique level-j branching node. This is the extra restriction that forces the spine, not just the equality of branch counts. It fixes the labelled-level hierarchy up to isomorphism, including h=1, where the three leaves form the whole structure. A quantifier-free formula depends only on its complete atomic type, proving the stated single existential-block test.
residual_risks: Replay exhausted 3, 18, 220, and 5,545 unlabelled hosts through the proposed minimum order at h=1,2,3,4, respectively. It found type totals 5,12,22,35 and exactly one winner at orders 3,5,7,9. This corroborates only those depths; the proof gives the unrestricted result.
The pure signature and fixed single existential block are essential to the stated consequence; no test for additional free relations or quantifier alternation is asserted.

evidence: The parity-game proof gives an intermediate bound g(ℓ,h)=Σ_{δ=1}^{ℓ} g(⌊ℓ/δ⌋,h−1) based on pruning by degrees, with g(ℓ,1)=ℓ and g(1,h)=1. At ℓ=3 the intermediate bound is exactly 2h+1. The two cited logic papers concern per-sentence satisfiability/complexity, not a least common host for all triple profiles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The published pruning proof works without order because appending δ children and inducing an embedding after pruning uses injective child maps, not their ordering. This yields the numerical lower bound for the unordered form as well; the weaker headline binomial bound should not be used for the comparison. The source's bound is not an equality classification. Broader logical signatures also do not imply simultaneous completeness or its equality cases.

evidence: The hierarchy is equivalently an ultrametric with merger levels as distances, or a depth-preserving unordered class tree. Embedding every unordered depth-h tree with at most three leaves is equivalent to profile universality. Directed orders of tuple coordinates do not add an order on the class-tree children. Ordering the comb's children side/spine/side gives an ordered (3,h)-universal tree, but the ordered requirement tests more embeddings. Bilet et al.'s three-point universality results concern inclusion-minimal real metric spaces.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The ultrametric and unordered tree aliases state the same question. A minimum ordered universal host can supply an unordered witness after forgetting order, but ordered minima or ordered rigidity alone make no assertion about all optimal hosts in the weaker unordered problem. Inclusion-minimality inside an ambient Euclidean space is not the least cardinality of a finite hierarchy.

originality.rationale: The genuine overlap with parity-game universal trees is substantial: the degree-threshold recurrence inside the proof of Czerwiński et al.'s Theorem 2.3 gives the numerical lower bound at three leaves, and the argument uses only properties valid also without order. Thus the numerical lower bound is not a new independent contribution, and the small universal comb is closely analogous to an ordered universal tree. The contribution surviving comparison is the equality classification of the weaker, unordered profile-universal problem: every minimum host is forced to have its branching vertices on one chain. The known size bounds and ordered universality results do not give this characterization of all unordered hosts. Simple profile counting and the logical rephrasing are not by themselves credited as new structural results.
residual_risks: The strongest overlap is the ordered-tree tradition and its degree-based bound, not the two logic papers. A standalone rigidity statement in the broader ordered/unordered universal-tree literature was not identified; priority for the equality classification remains provisional. No absence claim relies on a search miss.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md, mixed triple profiles and equality classification
value.rationale: For fixed merger levels one can ask which smallest hierarchies serve as a common fixture for every pure three-point test. The exact classification of all minimizers is a useful structural answer: having the necessary equilateral triples at every depth does not fix the fixture, whereas the mixed profiles force the spine. This is a uniform equality case for a motivated small-tree universality problem, not a sample census or just the specialization of the prior size recurrence.
residual_risks: The surviving contribution is a small structural rigidity lemma, not progress on general parity-game universal-tree bounds or on logical fragments with more variables. Profile counting and the existential reformulation alone would not establish value.
